summary: The revised plan addresses all three prior blocking issues and presents a comprehensive, well-structured implementation plan with proper task decomposition, clear acceptance criteria, and sound dependency ordering.
analysis: Reviewed the plan against all seven criteria. (1) Alignment with analysis: The plan now includes an Architecture Analysis Summary (lines 22-57) covering all three options with pros/cons, and the analysis artifact exists at .egg-state/drafts/1028-analysis.md. Option A (Embedded Coordinator) is selected with clear rationale. (2) Task breakdown: The previously oversized tasks (TASK-2-1, TASK-3-1, TASK-4-1) are now properly split into a/b subtasks. Each task targets 1-2 files and has a focused scope suitable for a single implementation pass. 22 tasks across 5 phases is well-granulated. (3) Acceptance criteria: Every task has testable criteria covering success paths, and dedicated test tasks (TASK-2-4, TASK-3-5, TASK-4-4, TASK-5-4) cover error paths explicitly. Criteria are specific — e.g., TASK-2-1a specifies guardrail enforcement and role validation rejection, not just 'works correctly'. (4) Dependency ordering: Phase 1 (foundation) → Phase 2 (APIs) → Phases 3 and 4 (parallel — executor/gateway and MCP server) → Phase 5 (instructions/integration). The parallelism between Phases 3 and 4 is correctly identified and justified. (5) Risk assessment: Eight risks identified with concrete mitigations. The coordinator crash scenario is handled (agents continue, optional respawn). Runaway spawning has numeric guardrails. MCP attack surface is mitigated by network isolation and token auth. (6) Test strategy: Four levels (unit, integration, backward-compat, edge cases) with specific scenarios. TASK-5-4 includes a workflow decision validation scenario, which is important for testing the coordinator's reasoning quality. (7) Completeness: All aspects covered including documentation (TASK-5-5), SSE integration (TASK-5-3), and the opt-in flag ensuring backward compatibility. The HITL decisions section (lines 59-127) is thorough — each of the 4 decisions and 3 feedback questions has an assumed default, affected tasks table, and description of how alternatives would change the implementation.
suggestions: 1. TASK-3-3 blocks `gh pr create` for the coordinator. Consider whether coordinator should be able to create PRs in edge cases (e.g., if no integrator agent exists). If not, document the rationale in the coordinator instructions (TASK-5-1) so the coordinator knows to delegate PR creation to an integrator or coder agent. 2. TASK-5-2 (container_spawner.py) should verify compatibility with the existing rules-merging pattern — the coordinator role is unique in that it needs cross-phase permissions, so the spawner logic may need a conditional path for coordinator vs. standard agent roles. 3. The yaml-tasks block at the end duplicates the prose. Consider whether the coder agent will use the yaml-tasks or the prose — if yaml-tasks is the authoritative source for the coder, ensure the prose stays in sync (or remove prose task details and keep only yaml-tasks). 4. TASK-1-4 mentions 'incremental updates (merge new state into existing)' — specify the merge strategy (shallow merge, deep merge, last-writer-wins for conflicts) to avoid ambiguity during implementation.
